lamina.name: Daily Activity
lamina.description: Daily activity and context: what a wearable measures, the energy the day is spending, and a first heart-rate model that separates resting level, circadian rhythm, heat and activity drive.

attribute.name: Measured Heart Rate
attribute.description: Mean measured heart rate in this minute. The one direct measurement of the quantity the rest of the chain models, so it is allowed to disagree with the model — that disagreement is what HR_residual reports.

attribute.name: Active Energy Rate
attribute.description: Active energy rate: the energy the day is spending above rest. Zero is a person sitting still, not a broken sensor, which is why the range starts there.

attribute.name: Basal Energy Rate
attribute.description: Basal energy rate: what the body spends at rest. Declared separately from activity so the model can name both halves instead of lumping them into one total.

attribute.name: Step Rate
attribute.description: Steps per minute. Shown as an input and used by no function yet: activity reaches the heart-rate model through AE_rate, and inventing a second path before the first is fitted would be putting arithmetic ahead of evidence.

attribute.name: Apparent Temperature
attribute.description: Outdoor apparent temperature, the temperature the person actually experiences rather than the one a weather station reports.

attribute.name: Local Clock Hour
attribute.description: Local clock hour, from 0 to 24. It drives the circadian term only; no function in this chain reads it as a date or a duration.

attribute.name: Tick Interval
attribute.description: Data time since the previous tick. Declared now because a rate integrated over the wrong interval is a confidently wrong total; no function in this phase reads it yet.

attribute.name: Resting Heart Rate Level
attribute.description: The slow personal resting level for the day — where this person's heart rate sits between circadian and activity drives. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Walking Workout Indicator
attribute.description: 1 during a minute the recording labels as Walking; 0 otherwise. In a scenario a preset or a slider sets it.

attribute.name: Strength Workout Indicator
attribute.description: 1 during a minute the recording labels as a strength workout; 0 otherwise. In a scenario a preset or a slider sets it.

attribute.name: Cardio Workout Indicator
attribute.replay_field: sample.workout in StairClimbing, Elliptical, Running, Cycling, HighIntensityIntervalTraining, Rowing
attribute.description: 1 during a minute the recording labels as a cardio workout; 0 otherwise. In a scenario a preset or a slider sets it.

attribute.name: Resting Level Offset
attribute.description: A constant this person's quiet heart rate sits away from HR_level. HR_level is the daily level of a resting marker computed elsewhere (for s2 about 76 bpm while measured heart rate reaches 44), so it is kept as given and not refitted; the offset is fitted instead, on quiet minutes outside workouts. Zero until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Maximum Heart Rate
attribute.description: Upper bound the model's target is clamped to. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Activity Drive Gain
attribute.description: Gain on the activity drive, in bpm per unit of raised energy rate. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Activity Drive Exponent
attribute.description: Exponent on the activity drive: below one, the first minutes of activity raise heart rate steeply and later minutes add less. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Walking Activity Gain
attribute.description: Multiplies the activity drive during a Walking workout; 1 means no different from any other activity. The baseline is a generic default; a fitted value belongs to ONE person and lives in that person's params.json beside their recordings, never in this file.

attribute.name: Strength Activity Gain
attribute.description: Multiplies the activity drive during a strength workout; 1 means no different from any other activity. The baseline is a generic default; a fitted value belongs to ONE person and lives in that person's params.json beside their recordings, never in this file.

attribute.name: Cardio Activity Gain
attribute.description: Multiplies the activity drive during a cardio workout; 1 means no different from any other activity. The baseline is a generic default; a fitted value belongs to ONE person and lives in that person's params.json beside their recordings, never in this file.

attribute.name: Circadian Amplitude
attribute.description: How far the circadian rhythm swings around the resting level. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Circadian Peak Hour
attribute.description: Local clock hour at which the circadian term peaks. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Heat Effect at Rest
attribute.description: Heart-rate rise per degree of apparent temperature above T_ref, at rest. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Reference Temperature
attribute.description: Temperature above which heat adds heart rate; below it the heat term is zero rather than negative, because mild cold is not modelled here. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Heart Rate Rise Time Constant
attribute.description: Time constant while heart rate rises toward its target. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Heart Rate Fall Time Constant
attribute.description: Time constant while heart rate falls toward its target. A seeded default until a fitted params.json replaces it.

attribute.name: Measured Heart Rate
attribute.description: The measured heart rate carried into the chain. It refuses a missing or non-finite reading rather than passing it on, so the engine marks it stale instead of letting a confident-looking value downstream hide the gap.

attribute.name: Total Energy Expenditure Rate
attribute.description: Energy spent per minute: activity plus basal. The sum is deliberately simple — no thermic effect of food, no exercise efficiency term — because those are corrections to fit later, not structure to guess now.

attribute.name: Estimated Oxygen Consumption
attribute.description: Energy rate converted to oxygen consumption. The conversion uses 4.86 kcal per litre of oxygen, which is an approximation: the accepted range is 4.69 to 5.05 depending on substrate, and 4.86 is a single stand-in for that spread.

attribute.name: Circadian Heart Rate Contribution
attribute.description: The circadian swing around the resting level: positive near the personal peak hour and negative half a day away from it.

attribute.name: Heat Heart Rate Contribution
attribute.description: Heart rate added by heat above the reference temperature. Floored at zero: this model knows that heat raises heart rate and does not claim that cold lowers it.

attribute.name: Activity Gain
attribute.depends_on: is_walk, is_strength, is_cardio, g_walk, g_strength, g_cardio
attribute.description: How much this minute's activity drive is scaled for the kind of workout it is. One means the workout kind makes no difference; a value away from one is this person's fitted response, selected by the indicator the recording set.

attribute.name: Activity Heart Rate Drive
attribute.description: Heart rate the current activity calls for, before it is added to the resting level, after the activity gain for the workout kind. The exponent makes the first minutes of activity count for more than later minutes at the same rate.

attribute.name: Target Heart Rate
attribute.description: The heart rate the model says this minute asks for: resting level plus circadian swing plus heat plus activity drive, clamped between 35 and the personal maximum.

attribute.name: Modelled Heart Rate
attribute.description: The target after the heart rate's own first-order lag. It approaches the target with tau_on while rising and tau_off while falling, so a step in activity shows up over minutes rather than instantly. After a stretch with no inputs it restarts at HR_target rather than pretending the last value is still current.

attribute.name: Heart Rate Residual
attribute.description: Measured heart rate minus modelled heart rate. Zero means the model explained the minute; a non-zero residual is the part of the day the declared drives do not account for, and the outcome this lamina reports.

attribute.name: Active Energy Today
attribute.description: Active energy accumulated since local midnight. A minute with no active-energy record adds nothing measured, so the total holds across a gap rather than inventing energy for a minute nobody recorded.

function.name: Measured Heart Rate
function.description: Carries the measured reading into the chain. A missing or non-finite reading is refused rather than passed along, so the engine marks HR_measured stale and nothing downstream mistakes an absent measurement for a value.

function.name: Total Energy Expenditure Rate
function.description: Activity energy plus basal energy, in kcal/min. The simplest defensible total: the corrections belong in a fitted model, not in arithmetic invented here.

function.name: Estimated Oxygen Consumption
function.description: Converts energy rate to oxygen consumption. 4.86 kcal per litre of oxygen is an approximation; the accepted range is 4.69 to 5.05, so this is an estimate whose error band is wider than the arithmetic suggests.

function.name: Circadian Heart Rate Contribution
function.description: One cosine around the 24-hour clock, peaking at the personal peak hour. It can be negative, because half a day from the peak is a genuine trough rather than an absence of rhythm.

function.name: Heat Heart Rate Contribution
function.description: Heat adds heart rate above the reference temperature and adds nothing below it. The floor is deliberate: this model does not claim a cooling effect it has not declared.

function.name: Activity Gain
function.inputs: is_walk, is_strength, is_cardio, g_walk, g_strength, g_cardio
function.description: Selects this person's gain for the kind of workout the minute is in. With no workout all three indicators are zero and the gain is one, so a minute that is not a workout is unchanged; a minute labelled as two kinds at once is refused rather than added.

function.name: Activity Heart Rate Drive
function.description: Activity energy turned into a heart-rate drive, scaled by the gain for this minute's workout kind. A negative AE_rate is refused rather than exponentiated: it is a unit or wiring error, and a fractional power of a negative number is not a heart rate. A gain of zero or less is refused for the same reason: it would report that activity drives the heart backwards or not at all.

function.name: Target Heart Rate
function.formula: HR_target = clamp(HR_level + HR_offset + HR_circ + HR_thermal + HR_drive, 35, HR_max)
function.inputs: HR_level, HR_offset, HR_circ, HR_thermal, HR_drive, HR_max
function.description: Sums the personal resting level, its fitted offset and the three declared drives, and clamps the result to the physiological floor and the personal maximum. The clamp is the model saying it can report a target no lower or higher than a heart can go, not a correction applied afterwards.

function.name: Modelled Heart Rate
function.formula: HR_model = prev + (1 - exp(-dt_s / tau)) * (HR_target - prev); tau = tau_on when HR_target > prev, else tau_off; prev = HR_target on the first tick and after a gap
function.description: Approaches the target with the heart rate's own first-order lag, using tau_on while rising and tau_off while falling. It is no longer the target reported unchanged: a step in activity arrives over minutes. After a stretch with no inputs it restarts at HR_target rather than carrying a stale value forward.

function.name: Heart Rate Residual
function.description: The measured value minus the modelled value. This is the lamina's outcome: it says how much of the minute the declared drives left unexplained, without pretending the model may correct the measurement.

function.name: Active Energy Today
function.formula: kcal_active_cum = prev + AE_rate * dt_s / 60; restarts at local midnight
function.description: Adds this minute's active energy to the running total and restarts it at local midnight. A minute with no active-energy record adds nothing measured, so the total holds across a gap rather than inventing energy nobody recorded.

composite.name: Heart Rate and Energy State
composite.description: What was measured, what the model expected, and the energy the day is spending.

segment.name: Activity and Context
segment.description: What the wearable measures, and the conditions the day arrives in
segment.attributes: HR_obs, AE_rate, BE_rate, step_rate, T_app, hour_local, dt_s, HR_level, is_walk, is_strength, is_cardio

segment.name: Personal Coefficients
segment.description: The seeded personal terms the heart-rate model reads. Defaults until a fitted params.json replaces them.
segment.attributes: HR_offset, HR_max, k_I, p_I, g_walk, g_strength, g_cardio, A_circ, phi_circ, k_T, T_ref, tau_on, tau_off

segment.name: Heart Rate and Energy
segment.description: The chain from measurement and energy to a modelled heart rate and the residual it leaves
segment.attributes: HR_measured, EE_total, VO2_est, HR_circ, HR_thermal, g_activity, HR_drive, HR_target, HR_model, HR_residual, kcal_active_cum
segment.functions: measured_hr, energy_total, vo2_estimate, hr_circadian, hr_thermal, activity_gain, hr_drive, hr_target, hr_model, hr_residual, kcal_cumulative

outcome.name: Target Heart Rate Residual
outcome.description: The model is considered adequate while the measured and modelled heart rates sit within 10 bpm of each other. The band is wide on purpose: this is an unfitted first model, and a residual inside it says the declared drives are plausible, not that they are right.
